question: How can qualification be both one and differentiated at the same time?
premises: At the level of reliance on the self-principle, qualification can be described as one.
Difference in preparation produces difference in qualification.
inference: Qualification is unitary in its basic locus but differentiated according to preparation.
uncertainties: saṃskārāśraya appears without an explicit case ending in the tokenized form; its relation is inferred from the compound context.
plain_english: Thus there is a single qualification insofar as all rely on the self-principle, yet qualification becomes differentiated because of differences in preparation.
